### Added
- **Mixed-tier portals are now priced correctly.** Sales and Service Hub are each
  priced at the tier their own seat values name, so a portal running one hub on
  Enterprise and another on Pro no longer prices every seat off a single guessed
  tier -- and it needs no configuration. The report names the mix and says which
  tiers it read and which it assumed. Pin `tier` or set `[<portal>.prices]` to
  remove the guess entirely.

### Fixed
- **A user holding two seats is no longer mistaken for a cheap one.** HubSpot lets
  one person hold a Sales and a Service seat in a single combined value. HubScan
  did not recognise it, ranked it as the cheapest seat possible, and could advise
  "upgrading" a portal's most expensive people to view-only while billing them at
  zero. They are now costed as both seats and counted against both. An
  unrecognised seat now ranks as expensive, so the next seat type HubSpot ships
  cannot repeat this.
- **Service Hub downgrade warning no longer skipped** for anyone holding a
  combined seat -- exactly the users it protects.
- **Recommendations table is colour-coded again** in the HTML report, so
  downgrades and upgrades stand out at a glance.
- **Reports no longer point the reader at an internal file** they cannot open.
  The caveats already say what they need to say on their own.
- **Release notes no longer carry client data.** This changelog ships verbatim to
  the public releases repo and to the in-app update banner, so client names could
  reach both. Released sections are now scrubbed, and a release fails if its notes
  carry a client name, a non-vendor email address, or run long.
